verdict.rationale: Firebase's own Cloud Firestore docs say it keeps data in sync across client apps through realtime listeners, and that apps can listen to data even offline. That is exactly a push-based subscription that removes the need to polling. Independent community reports confirm real-time sync to multiple clients (a whiteboard app) and quick addition of real-time notifications. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the listener API (query-level subscriptions, change-event types, detach/unsubscribe semantics) and Realtime Database listener specifics.

support.subject: As a developer, I can subscribe to live data changes so my UI updates in real time without polling

citations.quote: it keeps your data in sync across client apps through realtime listeners and offers offline support for mobile and web
Cloud Firestore caches data that your app is actively using, so the app can write, read, listen to, and query data even if the device is offline.

Built a real-time whiteboarding app for teachers on the original Firebase over 10 years ago. 'It was so fast I was able to build basic collision physics of letter tiles and have their positions sync to multiple clients at once.'
